verdict.rationale: Sill runs entirely on hardware you own. It has no account and no server, and the open-source Mac host can be built from source or run headless on the command line. Remote access goes through your own VPN or a forwarded port rather than a vendor relay. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of building and running a self-built host.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: There is no account and no server: your screen and what you type travel only between your own devices
Sill is free and open source.
`swift run -c release SillHost` runs the same host on the command line
This builds Sill.app with SwiftPM, signs it with your Apple Development identity, replaces /Applications/Sill.app and opens it.
Remote Access lets you use your Mac away from home, through your own VPN, such as Tailscale, or through a port you forward on your router.
